item.title: South Korea’s Key Policy Chief Kim Yong-Beom Steps Down
item.description: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung accepted the resignation of his chief policy secretary Kim Yong-beom Tuesday, according to the presidential Blue House.
item.dc:creator: Heesu Lee

item.title: Trump Says Pharma Companies Commit To Lowering Prices | Balance of Power: Late Edition 08/31/2026
item.description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Rep. Tim Moore (R-NC) says the votes are there to pass a continuing resolution that would keep the government open through mid-December. Rebecca Patterson, Senior Fellow at CFR and former Chief Investment Strategist for Bridgewater Associates, lays out four ways to bring down long-term bond yields: open the Strait of Hormuz, address the fiscal deficit, Treasury intervention, or an economic slowdown that no one wants. Dan Brouillette, former Energy Secretary during President Trump's first term, says additional Venezuelan oil will not lower US gas prices in the near term, arguing that the US needs more refining and pipeline capacity. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Burnham to Address UK Parliament as MPs Return From Summer Break
item.description: After a political honeymoon of good vibes and voter-friendly announcements, the return of Parliament means that the UK’s new prime minister, Andy Burnham, must confront hard choices that lie ahead.
item.dc:creator: Joe Mayes

item.title: Trump Floats Hollywood Tax Credits for US Film Industry
item.description: President Donald Trump called for a federal tax credit to benefit the movie and television industry, saying it would help bring the production of Hollywood blockbusters back to the US.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer A. Dlouhy

item.title: Brouillette: Venezuelan Oil Won't Lower Gas Prices Immediately
item.description: Dan Brouillette, former Energy Secretary during President Trump's first term, says additional Venezuelan oil will not lower US gas prices in the near term, arguing that the US needs more refining and pipeline capacity. Brouillette says he would not recommend investing in Venezuela at the moment and that companies need more certainty and details before committing significant capital. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Patterson: Congress Needs a More Fiscally Sustainable Path
item.description: Rebecca Patterson, Senior Fellow at CFR and former Chief Investment Strategist for Bridgewater Associates, lays out four ways to bring down long-term bond yields: open the Strait of Hormuz, address the fiscal deficit, Treasury intervention, or an economic slowdown that no one wants. Patterson adds that Congress needs to find a more fiscally sustainable path. She speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rep. Moore: 'Votes Are There' to Pass CR
item.description: Rep. Tim Moore (R-NC) says the votes are there to pass a continuing resolution that would keep the government open through mid-December. Rep. Moore says difficulty getting the 60 votes needed to advance legislation in the Senate has contributed to Congress’ reliance on continuing resolutions and says Washington spends too much as the national debt tops $40 trillion. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Army Secretary Driscoll Resigns After Clash With Hegseth
item.description: US Army Secretary Dan Driscoll is stepping down after repeated clashes with his boss, Pete Hegseth, leaving the service without several top leaders even as the conflict with Iran continues.
item.dc:creator: Jen Judson and Jennifer A. Dlouhy

item.title: Trump Says US Could Still 'Smack' Iran
item.description: President Donald Trump dismissed concerns that the conflict in Iran was draining American firepower, saying "This is a relatively little war for us." Bloomberg's Mica Soellner reports from the White House. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: India's Modi Calls on Putin to End War in Ukraine
item.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi called on President Vladimir Putin to end Russia’s war in Ukraine during a meeting in Kyrgyzstan. Putin responded that "we're moving in this direction." The meeting took place on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bessent Faces G20 Credibility Test | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 8/31/2026
item.description: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s interventionist summer has already led to pushback and questions about his credibility in financial markets. Now he faces a test with global peers. Ahead of the meeting of Group of 20 finance ministers in Asheville, North Carolina, on Monday, Bessent has vowed to return the conversation among the world’s top economic policymakers to the core subject of boosting growth. Shawn Donnan, Bloomberg Senior Economics Writer talks about the latest from the G20. Ed Ludlow, Bloomberg Tech Co-Host also discussed his interview with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Then, Brian Quintenz, KalshiEx Board Member and Fmr. CFTC Commissioner joined to discuss recent enforcement actions from the prediction market platform. Finally, Ryan Gould, Bloomberg News Deals Reporter discussed the latest on his reporting about how KKR has spent the past five years leveraging limited airport space to the advantage of Atlantic. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bessent Takes Trump’s Economic Pitch to a Skeptical G20
item.description: Allies question the US prescription for global growth.
item.dc:creator: Nancy Cook

item.title: Supreme Court Lets Trump Keep Building White House Ballroom
item.description: The US Supreme Court let President Donald Trump keep building his new White House ballroom for now, brushing aside conclusions by two lower courts that he is probably violating the law.
item.dc:creator: Greg Stohr and Zoe Tillman

item.title: Trump Adds Nine Drugmakers to Medicaid Price Deal Program
item.description: The Trump administration has struck new drug pricing agreements with nine biotech and pharmaceutical companies including UCB SA, Bridgebio Pharma Inc. and Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd.
item.dc:creator: Rachel Cohrs Zhang, Skylar Woodhouse and Nyah Phengsitthy

item.title: House Faces Tricky Midterm Agenda | Radio Balance of Power: Early Edition 8/31/2026
item.description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondents Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz discuss the latest between the US and Iran. On today's show, former US Army Europe Commanding General Ben Hodges, Stonecourt Capital Partner Rick Davis, Harvard Kennedy School Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino and Republican Congressman Rich McCormick of Georgia. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Russia's Putin Meets China's Xi, India's Modi in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin met with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit in Kyrgyzstan. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Dutch Government Clinches Budget Deal, Averting Political Crisis
item.description: The ruling Dutch coalition parties reached a last-minute agreement on its first annual budget, averting a fresh political crisis for centrist Prime Minister Rob Jetten’s six-month-old minority government.
item.dc:creator: Patrick Van Oosterom

item.title: South Korea’s Lee Shakes Up Cabinet to Restore Momentum
item.description: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung’s surprise cabinet overhaul appears aimed at strengthening his control of the policy agenda amid mounting public discontent over housing, justice and widening inequality despite an accelerating economy.
item.dc:creator: Soo-Hyang Choi

item.title: Trump Dismisses ‘Little War’ With Iran as Mideast Clashes Resume
item.description: President Donald Trump dismissed concerns that the conflict in Iran was draining American firepower as clashes resumed in the on-again off-again hostilities that have stretched more than six months, with neither side willing to restart negotiations to end the war.
item.dc:creator: Skylar Woodhouse and Omar Tamo

item.title: Senate Passes Funding Bill Ignoring Trump’s Priorities
item.description: The US Senate passed a short-term spending bill to avert a damaging government shutdown weeks before the November midterms, sidestepping President Donald Trump’s calls to also enact emergency funds for the Iran war and elements of a controversial voter identification proposal.
item.dc:creator: Erik Wasson
